messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  

This follows from the water phase diagram: as pressure falls below the triple‑point pressure (≈ 0.006 atm), the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward, so the temperature at which ice melts (or water freezes) becomes lower. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about –2 °C (≈ −3.6 °F).
